$documentation: Enumerated exceptions for the blocking dependency-audit gate (scripts/audit-gate.mjs,
run by the `audit` job in .github/workflows/test.yml). Policy narrative lives in
Every advisory `bun audit` reports must either be FIXED or appear here. There is no
third option and no global escape hatch: this file replaced a `continue-on-error` +
`|| echo` pair whose justification ('all in harper transitive deps') was true when it
was written, carried no expiry, and was still silently passing the build long after it
Adding an entry is a REVIEWED act, not a way to get green. Each one must carry the
advisory id, what pulls it in, why it cannot be fixed from this repo, a hard expiry
date, and the concrete condition that retires it. The gate enforces all of that
mechanically, including a severity-scaled cap on how long an entry may live — you
cannot park a critical for a year.
When an entry expires the build FAILS and a human re-decides. That is the mechanism
working. Re-dating an entry without re-reading its reason is how this file rots back

classes.no-patch-published: No fixed version exists on the registry yet. Verified by the gate on every run: if a patched version ships, this entry fails and must be actioned.
classes.vendor-pinned: A patched version exists upstream, but the vulnerable copy is resolved inside a vendored dependency whose tree we do not control. Retired by moving the vendor, not by bumping the leaf.
classes.remediation-available: A patched version exists AND we could take it. Deliberately deferred to a separate, test-gated dependency PR so a security gate lands independently of a lockfile change. Shortest leash of the three.

entries.reason: Resolved inside harper's pinned unreleased v5 build. @fastify/static 10.1.2 fixes it upstream, but the resolution belongs to harper's HTTP layer and overriding it globally would change the static-file server harper itself mounts. flair does not serve user-supplied paths through it.
entries.removeWhen: harper ships a v5 build resolving @fastify/static >=10.1.2, or flair stops depending on harper.

entries.reason: Same vendored edge and same upstream fix as GHSA-83w8-p2f5-377r; both clear when harper's pinned build moves to @fastify/static 10.1.2.
entries.removeWhen: harper ships a v5 build resolving @fastify/static >=10.1.2 — the same move that retires GHSA-83w8-p2f5-377r.

entries.introducedBy: harper -> lodash, and workspace @tpsdev-ai/n8n-nodes-flair -> n8n-workflow -> lodash
entries.reason: Two independent edges resolve the same vulnerable lodash, one of them inside harper's pinned build. lodash 4.18.1 fixes it, but a bun override is global — it would move harper's copy too, and lodash 4.18 is a minor bump across a package harper uses pervasively. The vulnerable API (_.template with attacker-controlled imports keys) is not reachable from flair's own code.
entries.removeWhen: harper ships a v5 build resolving lodash >=4.18.1 AND n8n-workflow does the same, or the n8n-nodes-flair workspace package is dropped. Both edges must clear.

entries.reason: No fixed release exists — the latest published validate.js is itself inside the vulnerable range, and the package is effectively unmaintained. It is also resolved inside harper's pinned build, so even a future fix arrives via harper rather than directly. ReDoS in a validator flair does not invoke.
entries.removeWhen: validate.js publishes a fixed release AND harper picks it up, or flair stops depending on harper. The gate flags the first half automatically.

entries.reason: mariadb is resolved only inside @mikro-orm/mariadb@6.6.16, which pins it exactly at 3.4.5; that pin is owned by @google/adk's non-optional peerDependencies, a tree we do not control. The patched 3.4.6 was never published (the 3.4 line stops at 3.4.5; latest is 3.5.3), so the only 'fix' is a major bump that violates mikro-orm's exact pin. mariadb IS present in the shipped @tpsdev-ai/adk-flair tree (verified: a fresh npm i @tpsdev-ai/adk-flair@0.50.0 --omit=dev contains mariadb@3.4.5) and absent from the @tpsdev-ai/flair CLI tree, which has no @google/adk edge. It is never loaded: @google/adk's sessions/db/operations.js requires @mikro-orm/mariadb only inside the mariadb:// URI branch, and adk-flair imports @google/adk type-only with no runtime import in dist/.
entries.removeWhen: If anything in dev or CI ever connects to a real MariaDB, or @google/adk starts eager-loading the driver (importing @mikro-orm/mariadb outside the mariadb:// branch), this entry is stale and must be re-reviewed. Re-check at each @mikro-orm/mariadb or @google/adk bump.

entries.reason: Same vendored edge as GHSA-cqhc-2h57-wpxf: mariadb is pinned at 3.4.5 by @mikro-orm/mariadb inside @google/adk's non-optional peers, and the patched 3.4.6 was never published. Cleartext transmission of credentials applies only when the connector is actually used, and the driver loads lazily only on an explicit mariadb:// URI that flair never issues.
entries.removeWhen: Same trigger as GHSA-cqhc-2h57-wpxf: any dev/CI connection to a real MariaDB, or @google/adk eager-loading the driver, retires this entry. Re-check at each @mikro-orm/mariadb or @google/adk bump.
